# Rook

> Rook is a paper trading desk for one trade at a time. It scans a session for
> setups, sizes a plan against written limits, and returns a verdict from a pure
> function that a model cannot influence. Every verdict — including every refusal —
> is journaled. No orders are placed, no account is connected, no custody exists.

Rook runs as a static React app with one Worker in front of it. State lives in the
browser; the Worker serves the session and runs the same risk gate the page runs.
The model is optional: with no key it still answers from the desk.

## Docs

- [index.md](/docs/index.md): what the desk does, the vocabulary, and what an agent may do here.
- [rules.md](/docs/rules.md): the fifteen gate rules, the verdict shape, and `POST /api/risk/check` with a worked example.
- [journal.md](/docs/journal.md): the record format (schema 2), its fields, its limits, and the export bundle.
- [ninth.md](/docs/ninth.md): the agent harness — routing, twelve skills, seventeen tools, budgets, stop reasons, slash commands.
- [skill.md](/docs/skill.md): the operating contract for an agent using this surface, including the refusal contract.

## Boundaries

- Paper only. Nothing on this surface places, routes or settles an order.
- The gate is a pure function. A model may explain a verdict; it may not produce one.
- Refusals are data. A blocked verdict carries a rule id and the numbers that failed.
- No accounts, no cookies, no server-side rows. The journal is the reader's browser.
